title: Iron considerations for the athlete: a narrative review
authors: Sim M, Garvican-Lewis LA, Cox GR, Govus A, McKay AKA, Stellingwerff T, Peeling P
population: Athletes (especially female and endurance athletes); review of iron regulation, hepcidin, sex hormones, diet, training and altitude
findings: Iron deficiency is commonly diagnosed in female and endurance athletes: about 15-35% of female athlete cohorts are deficient versus about 5-11% of male athlete cohorts.
Exercise-induced increases in the iron regulatory hormone hepcidin are highlighted as a contributor to altered iron metabolism in athletes.
The review covers effects of sex hormones, macronutrient manipulation, training and environmental stress (e.g. altitude hypoxia) on iron status and offers recommendations for consideration.
limitations: A narrative review, not a formal consensus statement (the brief's 'Sim 2019 consensus' label is inaccurate). The abstract gives no ferritin thresholds or dosing rules.
implications: Add an optional iron-status prompt for female and high-volume endurance users (user-entered latest ferritin). If fatigue or underperformance persists 2 or more weeks despite stable load (design default), suggest clinician blood testing. No self-supplementing advice.
No numeric training modification is justified; use as rationale for the flag, not a threshold.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (Eur J Appl Physiol, 2019-05, Sim). Prevalence figures confirmed in Europe PMC abstract (PMID 31055680).
